Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Primary assessment: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration (based on history of vomiting followed by watery diarrhoea, frequent stools, poor oral intake, and weakness)
- Supporting differential diagnoses (based on DDx consistent with transcript):
  - Viral gastroenteritis (High likelihood): Classic pattern of vomiting then watery diarrhoea; self-limited course; dehydration with reduced intake; no blood in stool
  - Dehydration/electrolyte disturbances (High likelihood): Significant fluid loss with 5–6 stools/day and poor intake; weakness
  - Bacterial gastroenteritis (Moderate likelihood): Acute watery diarrhoea; possible but less clearly supported by fever or specific exposure
  - Crohn’s disease / Ulcerative colitis (Low likelihood): Diarrhoea present but episode is acute (3 days) without typical features
  - Colorectal cancer (Low likelihood): Family history present but presentation is acute without alarm features
- Note: No contradictions between transcript and DDx; no conflicts noted

Management Plan
- Primary treatment: Oral rehydration with Dioralyte; maintain fluid intake
- Medications: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) for fever/weakness; dose/route/frequency not documented
- Activity/work: Continue off work for next day or two; avoid returning until diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours
- Follow-up: If not better next week, return for re-evaluation
- Diagnostics: No labs or imaging ordered at this time
- Referrals: Not currently indicated

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Viral gastroenteritis — High: Onset with vomiting, followed by watery diarrhoea; short duration; no blood in stool; dehydration present
- Dehydration/electrolyte disturbances — High: Significant fluid loss with poor oral intake and weakness
- Bacterial gastroenteritis — Moderate: Acute diarrhoea; could be bacterial but lacks clear exposure or fever
- Crohn’s disease / Ulcerative colitis — Low: Diarrhoea present but onset is very acute with no abdominal pain or systemic inflammatory features
- Colorectal cancer — Low: Family history; presentation not typical for cancer in this acute setting
